# Introduction

[AWS ParallelCluster](https://aws.amazon.com/hpc/parallelcluster/) is a framework for setting up HPC clusters on AWS. It takes a YAML file with all the necessary definitions, transforms it into CloudFormation and deploys it. It supports [Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/) as scheduler.

Posit Workbench supports Slurm as an HPC back end via the [Slurm Launcher](https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/job_launcher/slurm_plugin.html). An [earlier repository](https://github.com/sol-eng/aws-parallelcluster-rsw/) showed one way to integrate the two, with Workbench running on the head node. That approach works but has several shortcomings:

-   The head node already runs `slurmctld` and `slurmdbd`. Adding Workbench makes it even more of a single point of failure.
-   All user traffic is routed through the head node.
-   The head node also acts as NFS server for the cluster's shared file systems, adding load that can degrade the user experience or crash the node when resources are exhausted.

This repository documents a reference architecture that overcomes these shortcomings with a focus on high(er) availability, and contains everything needed to deploy it.

# The approach

Several ParallelCluster features make this possible:

-   [Login nodes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/LoginNodes-v3.html) (since 3.7.0). Workbench runs on a pool of login nodes behind a load balancer instead of on the head node.
-   Shared file systems on EFS instead of NFS exported by the head node (since 3.8.0), including `/home`.
-   [Custom AMIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/building-custom-ami-v3.html). When the cluster scales up, a new EC2 instance is provisioned. With all software baked into the AMI this takes about 4 minutes; installing software at boot time would make it considerably longer.

Workbench's own state lives in PostgreSQL (required for load balancing), users come from AWS SimpleAD, and two Application Load Balancers provide TLS and DNS names. Those auxiliary services are created with [Pulumi](https://www.pulumi.com/). See [Architecture](Architecture.qmd) for the full picture.

# Setup instructions

The deployment has three steps, each documented on its own page:

1.  Set up the auxiliary services (VPC lookup, SimpleAD, databases, load balancers, DNS, S3 bucket, users) with [Pulumi](Pulumi.qmd)
2.  Build a custom [AMI](AMI.qmd) (uses the S3 bucket and network created in step 1). You can skip this step if all sessions run in Apptainer containers; see [When you need it](AMI.qmd#sec-ami-needed).
3.  Deploy the cluster with [AWS ParallelCluster](AWSParallelcluster.qmd)

If something does not work as expected, see [Troubleshooting](Troubleshooting.qmd).
